text: {"lessons":["Trimming winners in small increments can realize gains while preserving some upside, but I should set clear position-size and rebalancing rules rather than sell automatically whenever I’m ahead of cost.","I should judge trades by expected return, risk, and portfolio balance—not by average cost or the emotional satisfaction of locking in a gain; selling a winner can mean missing further growth.","Repeated buying and selling can undermine a coherent plan. Before each trade, I should identify what has changed, check cash and concentration, and avoid reacting to short-term price moves."]}
